note: Utilities, territories and customers from EIA-861 2024. County customer splits between utilities are estimates. Territories are whole counties merged, so they overlap where utilities share a county. Load zones are approximate. Eligible homes split each county's owner-occupied single-family homes by the estimated utility shares.

layers.label: Peak demand
layers.unit: MW, estimated 2024 summer peak (each utility's peak split by its customers)
layers.method: EIA-861 utility summer peak; wires companies without one get ERCOT weather-zone peak x their share of zone customers. Split to counties by estimated customers. Non-coincident peaks.

layers.label: Price spikes
layers.unit: hours per year at or above $1,000/MWh in the county's load zone (average)
layers.method: Mean annual hours with real-time settlement point price >= $1,000/MWh per load zone. County load zones are approximate.

layers.label: Long outages
layers.unit: hours per customer per year in outages lasting 12 hours or more (estimate)
layers.method: EAGLE-I 15-minute county outage counts cut into events; per-home durations assume the same homes stay dark while the count is above them. All dark hours of outages lasting 12 h or more, divided by modeled customers and years reporting.

layers.label: Flood
layers.unit: flood, flash-flood and coastal-flood event-days per year (NOAA, 2000-2025)
layers.method: Rank = mean of the Texas ranks of NOAA flood event-days per year and FEMA NRI's flood risk score (larger of inland and coastal). Demo counties also show FEMA flood-zone maps and the share of land in the 1% annual-chance floodplain.

layers.label: Tornadoes
layers.unit: EF-weighted tornado path km per thousand km² per year (2000-2025)
layers.method: NOAA SPC tracks split between the counties they cross (straight line start to end); each km weighted by EF rating + 1 (unknown = EF0), divided by county land area and years.

layers.label: Hail and wind
layers.unavailable_reason: Not built yet: NOAA SPC hail and wind reports (UM-4.2)

layers.label: Hurricanes
layers.unit: tropical-storm-force passes within 100 km per decade, weighted by wind (1980-2025)
layers.method: NHC best tracks interpolated hourly. Each storm whose 34 kt+ winds passed within 100 km of the county's interior point counts its strongest wind there ÷ 64 kt (a hurricane-force pass = 1).

layers.label: Winter freeze
layers.unavailable_reason: Not built yet: NOAA Storm Events (UM-5.1)

layers.label: Extreme heat
layers.unavailable_reason: Not built yet: NOAA Storm Events (UM-5.1)

layers.label: Weather hazard (FEMA)
layers.unit: FEMA NRI risk score, 0-100 (mean of winter, ice, hurricane, wind, tornado, heat)
layers.method: Mean of six FEMA NRI hazard risk scores. Stands in until the event-based hazard layers ship.

layers.label: Homes exposed
layers.method: ACS 5-year table B25032, owner-occupied one-unit homes by county.

scoring.rank_method: (average tie rank - 1) / (n valid - 1); null when fewer than 2 values

sources.name: EIA-861 2024 utility service territories and customers
Base Power pricing and offer pages
FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (effective flood maps)
NOAA SPC Severe Weather Database (tornado tracks)
NOAA NHC HURDAT2 Atlantic best tracks
ERCOT hourly native load by weather zone
